subject.title: [codex] Keep full-auto Codex exec from stale relay decline

question: Should missing, expired, or stale native-relay state be treated as non-authoritative only for the documented full-auto Codex posture, while explicit relay denials and direct OpenClaw hooks remain authoritative?
rationale: This intentionally converts selected fail-closed relay failures into command continuation at an execution-approval boundary, and tests alone do not establish the desired operational security policy.

options.title: Approve the bounded exception
options.body: Confirm the exact full-auto-only policy after paired live proof shows unavailable-relay execution and explicit-denial blocking.

options.title: Keep relay failures blocking
options.body: Retain fail-closed behavior and instead repair relay lifecycle or registration so full-auto runs do not encounter unavailable state.

recommendation.body: Confirm the exact full-auto-only policy after paired live proof shows unavailable-relay execution and explicit-denial blocking.
